Theme

Latin word

intersum

intersum, interesse, interfuī

verb, irregular (sum); with the dative, conjugation

be present at, attend; take part in, be present at

In this lexicon

  • attend

    the recommended word · classical · Tac. Dial. 34.2–3: hujus omnibus dictiōnibus interesse; Traupman 127: saltātiōnī intererō; M-O s.v. attend, take (a class, course): lēctiōnibus interesse

  • be involved

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 1.6.1: omnibus negōtiīs nōn interfuit sōlum, sed praefuit; Cic. Att. 14.22.2: cōnsiliīs (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • hunc sectārī, hunc prōsequī, hujus omnibus dictiōnibus interesse … adsuēscēbat

    He would get used to following him about, escorting him, being present at all his speeches.Tac. Dial. 34.2–3

    In the entry for attend

  • Lūcifer ambōrum nātālibus adfuit īdem: ūna celebrāta est per duo lība diēs

    The same morning star was there at both our births: one day was kept with two birthday cakes.Ov. Tr. 4.10.11–12

    In the entry for attend

  • Crās convīviō intereris?

    Will you be at the dinner tomorrow?composed

    In the entry for attend

  • quī nōn sōlum interfuit iīs rēbus, sed etiam praefuit

    who was not only involved in these matters but in charge of themCic. Fam. 1.8.1
